title: Retro runbook scaffolder with sampled trace rehydration and metric-context bundling
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Background: When SLO breaches or PagerDuty escalations occur we need a deterministic, low-friction way to assemble a compact incident evidence bundle and a first-draft runbook so on-call can act quickly and postmortems aren't delayed by manual artifact collection. Current tooling attaches traces or logs separately; engineering spends 10-30 minutes collecting context for medium-severity incidents. Goal: build an automated 'retro runbook scaffolder' that uses lightweight sampled tracing hooks at runtime to rehydrate full context when an incident signal arrives, bundles top spans + metric deltas + log snippets, and emits a templated runbook and postmortem draft attached to the PD/Slack incident thread.
technical_approach: 1) Runtime tracing hooks: add an opt-in incident metadata header (X-RD-INCIDENT) that is set by PD/Slack adaptor when creating an escalation. Tracing sidecars will mark in-process requests with incident-id and increase local trace sampling for those traces (ephemeral bump). 2) Sampling & rehydration policy: baseline sampling 0.5%-1% for production traffic; when an incident-id is present or SLO anomaly detected, trigger rehydration flow to pull full traces and related logs for requests with same trace_id or request_id in a +/- 5s window. 3) Evidence assembler service: collects top N spans (by self-time), aggregates error stacktraces, correlates metric time-series (p50/p95/p99 deltas vs baseline), and grabs up to 3 log snippets per span using indexed log-store queries. 4) Runbook scaffolder: use templates with sections (Summary, Timeline, Hypotheses, Immediate Mitigation, Next Steps, Data Links). Populate top 5 hypotheses using a lightweight span-rule engine (e.g., DB timeouts, gc, kernel saturation). 5) Integrations: post scaffold as a draft to PagerDuty incident notes and create a pinned Slack thread message with action buttons (Add Note / Start RCA / Mark Resolved) that call Redwood Console endpoints. 6) Storage and retention: bundles saved to secure evidence bucket with 30-day TTL and access controlled via RBAC/KMS. 7) Feature-flagged rollout with canary and fallbacks (disabled if evidence assembly exceeds 2 minutes or bundle size > 50MB).
tradeoffs_and_decisions: - Cost vs fidelity: default sampling remains low to control storage/ingestion costs; rehydration is triggered only on incidents/SLO anomalies to avoid full-fidelity capture. - Privacy & security: evidence bundles may contain PII; we will sanitize logs via existing log-filter pipeline and enforce KMS encryption on S3. - Latency: do not block incident routing on evidence assembly. PD/Slack attachments should appear immediately (a minimal placeholder) and be enriched asynchronously. - Complexity vs reliability: implemented as a separate service to avoid coupling runtime agents with heavy downstream logic; runtime only marks incident IDs and performs ephemeral sampling policy change.
acceptance_criteria: When a PagerDuty incident is opened with severity >= P2 and tagged 'infra' or 'runtime', a draft runbook is created and attached to the PD incident within 2 minutes

Draft must include: incident summary, top 5 spans (name + self-time), top 3 log snippets per span, metric percentiles (p50/p95/p99) for the affected service and baseline comparison, and links to raw traces/logs
Slack incident thread receives scaffold message with action buttons and a link to the evidence bundle
Evidence bundle size under 50MB for 95% of incidents and stored with 30-day TTL and KMS encryption
E2E test: synthetic incident triggers full flow in staging and verification checks the scaffold content automatically
Feature flag toggle allows rollback to zero impact within 15 minutes and telemetry reports assembly failures and latencies
implementation_steps: Design review and security sign-off (Confluence doc link in attachments)
Add runtime header and incident-id propagation to serving runtime (small API change)
Implement sampling policy change hook in tracing sidecar
Build evidence-assembler microservice and runbook templater
Add PD/Slack adaptor updates to attach drafts and provide action callbacks
E2E test harness for synthetic incidents and canary rollout to 10% of traffic
Monitor cost and failure metrics for 2 weeks before broad rollout
test_plan: Unit tests for span selection, log snippet extraction, metric aggregation rules
Integration tests: simulate incidents in staging and validate bundle contents and PD/Slack attachments
Load test: generate parallel incidents to exercise evidence assembler and enforce bundle size limits
Security test: verify KMS encryption, RBAC permissions, and PII redaction on extracted logs
rollout_plan: Gate behind 'retro-runbook' FF. Start with internal SRE + three customer pilot teams, then 10% canary across non-critical clusters for 48h. Observe assembly latency, bundle sizes, PD attach rates and any false positives. If assembly latency > 2 minutes or error rate > 3%, rollback the flag. Full rollout depends on cost telemetry and security sign-off.
monitoring_and_metrics: Track: scaffold_creation_latency_ms, evidence_bundle_size_bytes (p50/p95/p99), scaffold_failure_rate, pct_incidents_with_bundle, cost_per_incident_usd. Create dashboard in Console: 'Retro Runbook - Health' and alert if failure_rate > 2% or average assembly latency > 90s.
operational_runbook: If scaffold fails to assemble: 1) PD auto-notify oncall with link to minimal diagnostic snapshot, 2) fallback: attach raw trace links and metric snapshots, 3) run 'evidence-assembler' restart playbook and check queue length and downstream storage permissions. Documented in attachments.
